title: Reservoir leasing and pluggable shedder framework for Dedicated fleets
creator: Lucas Rivera
description: Introduce a reservoir leasing layer plus a pluggable shedder abstraction to provide deterministic per-tenant throughput contracts and graceful overload behavior for Dedicated fleets. This work combines a reservation/lease lifecycle, non-blocking queue semantics for short waits, and a modular shedder that can implement strategies such as soft-drop, token-delay, or staged-demotion depending on tenant SLA and fleet health.
background: Current Dedicated routing uses coarse admission heuristics and global shedder heuristics that cause variable tail latency and unpredictable tenant throughput during sudden load spikes. We need a deterministic mechanism that can: 1) reserve short-term throughput for contracts (min guarantees), 2) allow controlled bursts without breaking SLOs, and 3) apply configurable shedding strategies per tenant or service class. Prior tickets (ENG-24109, ENG-31567) explored queued backpressure and graceful absorption; this ticket unifies those ideas with a lease-based reservoir and a pluggable shedder API.
design_decisions: Use a time-windowed lease (lease TTL 1s by default) to express short-term throughput guarantees; leases are cheap to renew and are storable in the fleet coordinator cache.
Implement reservoir accounting per-fleet and per-priority-class; reservoirs hold a token budget that is replenished by autoscaler hints and admission feedback.

Expose a shedder interface (ShedderV1) with three canonical strategies: soft-drop (probabilistic), token-delay (queue with timeout promotion), staged-demotion (downgrade to lower-cost model or fallback path).
Admission decisions are made in two phases: fast-path (local cached lease check) and slow-path (coordinator reconciliation). Fast-path must be lock-free and bounded to <200us.
Default policy: honor min-throughput leases, permit short burst leases up to burst-capacity, and apply soft-drop once reservoir headroom is exhausted.
Keep telemetry at token and request level to compute per-tenant effective throughput, drop rates, and average latency; hook into Console metrics and SLO alerts.
Design for eventual rollout to Private deployments; shedder implementations must avoid centralized state where possible.
implementation_notes: Coordinator changes: add LeaseManager actor that tracks short-lived leases and provides a compact hash state for routers.
Router changes: add ReservoirLeaseChecker with atomic snapshot reads from coordinator cache; on miss, fall back to conservative admit/deny with slow-path async reconciliation.
Autoscaler integration: autoscaler will publish headroom hints (tokens/sec) per-fleet; LeaseManager will translate hints into reservoir replenishments.
Shedder interface: define Go/TypeScript interfaces and gRPC hook for remote shedder evaluation to support policy-as-code in the future.
Persistence: leases are ephemeral and do not require durable storage; however coordinator must persist last-known reservoir-size for safe restart warmup.
Backwards compatibility: routers without the new LeaseManager will continue to use existing admission code path; feature flag gating required.
Testing: create a synthetic tenant-workload harness that can replay burst patterns from real production traces (link below).
acceptance_criteria: Baseline: no regression in p50/p95 latency on a 100-tenant sanity run compared to current mainline.
Functional: lease lifecycle (acquire, renew, expire) observed in logs and metrics; renewals < 250us on fast-path.
SLO: under a 4x sudden traffic spike, tenants with min-guarantees retain >= 95% of their guaranteed throughput while best-effort tenants see graceful shedding.
Observability: Console shows per-tenant reservoir size, drop-rate, and shedder decision histogram; alerts for reservoir depletion firing correctly.
Rollout: feature flag rollout with automated canary that ramps from 1% to 50% traffic with no critical alerts for 48 hours.
Code quality: unit and integration tests covering edge cases (coordinator restart, lease drift, clock skew) and a benchmark demonstrating headroom recovery.
Security: shedder gRPC endpoint requires mTLS and token auth; security review completed if security_review_required is true.
Docs: PRD and Ops runbook published with rollback instructions and diagnostic queries.
Migration: no mandatory tenant migration required; default policy is backward compatible and off by feature flag.
Performance: incremental CPU overhead on router < 6% at 95th percentile for typical workloads.
Release: merged to release branch and scheduled in dedicated-2026.03 for gradual rollout.
Stakeholder sign-off: PM, SRE, and Design approvals recorded in comments.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal e2e test in staging with synthetic 200-tenant traffic profile (2 days).
2) Canary A: enable feature flag for 1% of production fleet (12 hours monitor), rollback if drop-rate > 2x baseline or critical alerts.
3) Canary B: 10% traffic with autoscaler hints enabled (24 hours), validate throughput contracts for reserved tenants.
4) Ramp to 50% over 72 hours if metrics stable; enable staged-demotion shedder for a small tenant subset.
5) Full enable after 7 days of stable behavior and SRE sign-off; schedule postmortem check-ins at 1d, 7d, 30d.
Rollback plan: toggle off feature flag and trigger coordinator state flush; ensure leases expire within TTL+1s and routers revert to legacy admit behaviour.
Communication: notify on-call, account success managers for impacted tenants, and publish a short note in #dedicated-capacity channel.
Playbooks: add diagnostic runbook entries and common mitigation steps (throttle tenant, split tenant, increase reserved capacity).
test_plan: unit tests for LeaseManager accounting and expiry semantics
integration test with Router+Coordinator and a simulated autoscaler publishing headroom hints
chaos test: restart coordinator mid-burst and validate no double-counting or phantom leases
load test: replay production spike traces to confirm throughput guarantees and shedder behavior
security test: verify mTLS and token auth for shedder RPCs
benchmark: measure CPU and latency overhead at target fleet scale (500 routers)
